title: Ingeniería
blurb: Fuerzas, máquinas y las formas que mantienen en pie las estructuras.

lessons.title: Fuerzas, palancas y engranajes
lessons.summary: Por qué funciona una llave larga y cómo las máquinas cambian fuerza por distancia.

cards.title: Fuerza, masa y peso
cards.text: Una fuerza hace que una masa acelere. El peso no es más que la fuerza de la gravedad sobre una masa: W = m × g, con g ≈ 9,81 m/s² en la Tierra. La masa se mide en kg; la fuerza y el peso, en newtons (N).

deep.x: Mass is how much matter something contains; weight is the force gravity exerts on that mass. In everyday speech they're mixed up, but engineers keep them apart.
Same mass, different weight

v.unit: weight of a 70 kg person, N

deep.x: Newton's second law
Units

items.b: force to accelerate 1 kg by 1 m/s²

deep.x: Why it matters
Structures and machines must carry weights (forces), so engineers convert masses to newtons before any calculation.
Mass is in kilograms; weight is a force, in newtons.

cards.title: Las palancas multiplican la fuerza
cards.text:
El efecto de giro, o par (momento), es la fuerza × la distancia al punto de apoyo. Una fuerza pequeña lejos del apoyo equilibra una fuerza grande cerca de él.

Por eso una llave larga afloja un tornillo atascado, y por eso los pomos de las puertas están lejos de las bisagras.

deep.x: A lever is a rigid bar that rotates around a pivot. The turning effect of a force (its moment or torque) is force times distance from the pivot.
Balancing

x: 600 N child at 1 m vs adult pushing at 3 m

deep.x: Three classes of lever

items.b: effort in middle: tweezers, your forearm

deep.x: Everyday levers
Archimedes is said to have boasted, "Give me a place to stand, and I will move the Earth", capturing the power of a long enough lever.

cards.title: Pruébalo: equilibra el balancín
cards.text: El lado derecho tiene 6 kg a 1 m del punto de apoyo. Cambia la masa y la distancia del lado izquierdo hasta que la barra quede nivelada.

deep.x: A seesaw balances when the moments on each side are equal. Mass alone doesn't decide it: distance from the pivot matters just as much.
The challenge

x: Left options: 3 kg at 2 m, 2 kg at 3 m, 12 kg at 0.5 m

deep.x: Several masses
With more than one mass on a side, add their moments: the total on each side must be equal.
Real seesaws
Mass times distance on one side must equal mass times distance on the other.

cards.title: Las poleas cambian distancia por fuerza
cards.text:
Con una polea móvil, la carga cuelga de dos tramos de cuerda, así que cada tramo soporta la mitad del peso. Tiras con la mitad de fuerza, pero tienes que tirar del doble de cuerda.

El trabajo que haces, fuerza × distancia, sigue siendo el mismo. Las máquinas nunca regalan energía; te dejan elegir cómo gastarla.
cards.sketch: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g class="d"><path class="s" d="M20 20L300 20"/><path class="s" d="M40 20L32 12"/><path class="s" d="M58 20L50 12"/><path class="s" d="M76 20L68 12"/><path class="s" d="M94 20L86 12"/><path class="s" d="M112 20L104 12"/><path class="s" d="M130 20L122 12"/><path class="s" d="M148 20L140 12"/><path class="s" d="M166 20L158 12"/><path class="s" d="M184 20L176 12"/><path class="s" d="M202 20L194 12"/><path class="s" d="M220 20L212 12"/><path class="s" d="M238 20L230 12"/><path class="s" d="M256 20L248 12"/><path class="s" d="M274 20L266 12"/><path class="s" d="M292 20L284 12"/><path class="s" d="M144 20L144 32"/><circle class="s" cx="144" cy="50" r="18"/><circle class="s" cx="180" cy="125" r="18"/><path class="a" d="M198 20 V125 A18 18 0 0 1 162 125 V50 A18 18 0 0 0 126 50 V150"/><path class="s" d="M180 143L180 150"/><rect class="s bgf" x="160" y="150" width="40" height="24" rx="3"/><path class="r" d="M110 120L110 162"/><path class="r" d="M106.5 154.8L110 162L113.5 154.8"/></g><text class="r" x="102" y="150" text-anchor="end" style="font-size:17px">tira 1 m</text><text class="" x="208" y="168" text-anchor="start" style="font-size:16px">carga sube ½ m</text></svg>

deep.x: Pulleys redirect and divide forces. With movable pulleys, the load is shared between several rope segments, so you pull with less force but over a longer distance.
Energy is conserved

items.s: Half the force, twice the distance

x: Lift 100 kg by 1 m with MA 4

deep.x: Friction
Real pulleys lose some energy to friction in the bearings and rope bending, so actual force is a bit higher than the ideal.
Where you see them
Machines trade force for distance; they never create energy.

cards.title: Engranajes: velocidad o par
cards.text:
Cuando un engranaje pequeño mueve uno grande, el grande gira más despacio pero con más par. La relación es el número de dientes: 10 dientes moviendo 20 dan la mitad de velocidad y el doble de par.

La marcha corta de una bici, la caja de cambios de un taladro y la primera marcha de un coche usan este intercambio.

deep.x: Gears transmit rotation between shafts. Their teeth ratio sets a trade-off between speed and torque.

v.f: Gear ratio = teeth on driven gear ÷ teeth on driver

deep.x: Example

x: Half the speed, twice the torque

deep.x: Everyday gears

items.b: small front, big rear: easy climbing
big front, small rear: fast on flats

deep.x: Gear types
Ancient gears
The Antikythera mechanism, an ancient Greek device from around 100 BC, used dozens of bronze gears to predict astronomical positions.
Gears let you choose: speed or force.

cards.title: Fuerzas equilibradas y desequilibradas
cards.text: Cuando las fuerzas sobre un objeto se equilibran, este sigue quieto o se mueve a velocidad constante. Cuando no, acelera en la dirección de la fuerza resultante.

deep.x: Newton's first law: an object stays at rest or moves at constant velocity unless a net force acts on it.
Examples

items.b: engine force balances drag and friction

deep.x: Free-body diagrams

steps: Draw every force acting on it

deep.x: Engineering use
Static structures must have balanced forces at every joint, or they would move.
Balanced forces don't mean no forces; they mean no net force.

cards.title: Planos inclinados
example: Subir 100 kg 1 m con una rampa de 4 m
cards.text: Una rampa te permite subir una carga con menos fuerza empujándola a lo largo de una distancia mayor. La fuerza necesaria es aproximadamente el peso por la altura dividido por la longitud.

deep.x: A ramp lets you raise a load using less force by spreading the work over a longer distance.
Example
Steeper vs longer
Accessibility
Building rules limit wheelchair ramp slopes, typically to around 1:12 or gentler, so people can push themselves up comfortably.
History
Ancient builders likely used ramps to raise stones for pyramids and temples, trading distance for force.
A ramp makes lifting easier by making the journey longer.

cards.title: Tornillos y cuñas
cards.text: Un tornillo es una rampa enrollada alrededor de un cilindro: cada vuelta lo hace avanzar un poco con mucha fuerza. Una cuña (un hacha, un cincel) convierte un empuje en una fuerza lateral que parte el material.

deep.x: Screws and wedges are variations of the inclined plane that produce large forces.
Screw advantage

x: Screw jack with 5 mm pitch, 30 cm handle
Handle travels about 1.9 m per turn

deep.x: Wedges
Axes, chisels, knives and doorstops turn a push into sideways splitting or holding forces. Thinner wedges split more easily but are weaker.
Archimedes' screw
Still used to pump water and move grain.
A screw is a long ramp you climb by turning.

cards.title: Ventaja mecánica

viz.f: VM = fuerza de salida ÷ fuerza de entrada

cards.text: La ventaja mecánica es la fuerza de salida dividida por la fuerza de entrada. Una palanca con VM = 5 te permite levantar 5 veces lo que empujas, pero te desplazas 5 veces más.

deep.x: Mechanical advantage (MA) measures how much a machine multiplies force. The price is distance.

items.m: Ideal MA = input distance ÷ output distance

deep.x: Examples
Efficiency
Velocity ratio
Engineers sometimes use velocity ratio: how much farther the input moves than the output. For frictionless machines, MA equals velocity ratio.
More force out always means more distance in.

cards.title: El par en la práctica
cards.text: Los tornillos se aprietan a un par especificado en newtons-metro. La tuerca de una rueda de coche suele estar en torno a 100–140 N·m: 400 N sobre una llave de 30 cm dan 120 N·m.

deep.x: Torque is how bolts are tightened correctly. Too little and they loosen; too much and threads strip or bolts snap.
Example

x: = 120 N·m: a typical car wheel nut

deep.x: Typical torques
Torque wrenches
A torque wrench clicks or signals when the set torque is reached. Critical bolts (wheels, cylinder heads, structural joints) should always be tightened this way.
Sequence
The manual's torque value isn't a suggestion.

Un engranaje de 12 dientes mueve uno de 36 dientes. La salida gira…
quiz.explain: La relación es 36 ÷ 12 = 3: un tercio de la velocidad y el triple de par.

lessons.title: Cómo se sostienen las estructuras
lessons.summary: Tracción, compresión y las formas que usan los ingenieros para controlarlas.

cards.title: Tracción y compresión
cards.text:
Carga una viga en el centro y se flexiona. La parte superior se comprime (compresión) y la inferior se estira (tracción). En algún punto intermedio hay una línea neutra que no sufre ninguna de las dos.

El hormigón resiste bien la compresión pero mal la tracción; por eso las vigas llevan barras de acero cerca de la parte inferior.

deep.x: Structures resist loads through two basic internal forces: tension (pulling apart) and compression (pushing together).
In a beam
Reinforced concrete
Concrete is strong in compression but weak in tension, so steel bars are placed where tension occurs, usually near the bottom of beams. Joseph Monier patented reinforced concrete ideas in the 1860s.
Materials by strength
Know where the tension is, and you know where the steel goes.

cards.title: Por qué a los ingenieros les encantan los triángulos
cards.text:
Empuja la esquina de un marco cuadrado y se pliega en un paralelogramo; las uniones simplemente giran. Un triángulo no puede cambiar de forma sin cambiar la longitud de un lado.

Por eso las grúas, las cerchas de tejado, las torres eléctricas y los cuadros de bici están hechos de triángulos.

deep.x: A triangle is the only polygon that can't change shape without changing a side's length. That makes it inherently rigid.
Trusses
Truss types
Bracing
Square frames can be made rigid by adding one diagonal brace, turning them into two triangles. That's why buildings use cross-bracing.
The Eiffel Tower (1889) is a giant lattice of triangles, using about 7,300 tonnes of iron for a 300-metre structure.

cards.title: Los arcos empujan hacia fuera
cards.text:
Un arco convierte una carga hacia abajo en compresión que recorre su curva hasta el suelo. La piedra, que resiste muy bien la compresión, es perfecta para ello.

El problema es que los pies empujan hacia fuera. Sin estribos sólidos o un tirante entre los pies, el arco se abre y se derrumba.

deep.x: An arch turns downward loads into compression that flows around its curve to the supports. It's ideal for stone, which is strong in compression.
The outward thrust

items.w: Arch built on weak supports
items.r: Solid abutments or a tie between the feet

deep.x: Famous arches
Águas Livres
Lisbon's Águas Livres Aqueduct, completed in the 18th century, has stone arches about 65 m tall across the Alcântara valley. It survived the 1755 earthquake.
Keystone
The central stone at the top locks the arch. Builders support arches on wooden frames (centring) until the keystone is placed.
Arches turn weight into compression, and push sideways to do it.

cards.title: La viga en I
cards.text:
Cuando una viga se flexiona, la mayor tensión está en las caras superior e inferior y muy poca en el centro. Una viga en I concentra la mayor parte del acero en las alas superior e inferior y las une con un alma delgada.

Consigues casi la rigidez de un bloque macizo con una fracción del peso.

deep.x: When a beam bends, stress is greatest at the top and bottom and lowest near the middle. The I-beam puts material where it works hardest.
Parts

items.b: top and bottom plates: carry most bending stress
vertical plate: carries shear, separates flanges

deep.x: Efficiency

v.unit: relative stiffness for the same weight (illustrative)

deep.x: Hollow sections
Tubes and box sections also place material far from the centre and resist twisting better than I-beams.
Put the material where the stress is.

cards.title: Factor de seguridad
cards.formula: FS = carga de rotura ÷ carga de trabajo
cards.text:
Los ingenieros nunca diseñan justo hasta el punto de rotura. Los materiales varían, las cargas se subestiman y las cosas se desgastan. El factor de seguridad indica cuánto más resistente es algo de lo que necesita ser.

Los equipos de elevación suelen usar 4 o 5; las estructuras de los aviones usan alrededor de 1,5, porque el peso extra cuesta combustible y cada pieza se inspecciona a fondo.
example: Gancho para 1 t, rompe a 4 t
cards.sketch: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g class="d"><rect class="fpen" x="30" y="56" width="70" height="26" rx="3"/><rect class="fred" x="30" y="104" width="280" height="26" rx="3"/></g><text class="a" x="110" y="75" text-anchor="start" style="font-size:17px">nominal 1 t</text><text class="tp" x="40" y="123" text-anchor="start" style="font-size:17px">rompe a 4 t</text><text class="" x="160" y="165" text-anchor="middle" style="font-size:18px">4 ÷ 1 = factor de seguridad 4</text></svg>

deep.x: Engineers never design right to the breaking point. The factor of safety covers uncertainties in loads, materials, manufacturing and wear.

v.f: Factor of safety = failure load ÷ design load

deep.x: Typical values
Why so different

items.b: weight costs fuel, parts tested and inspected
shock loads, wear, human life at risk
codes apply partial factors to loads and materials

deep.x: Partial factors
Modern codes like Europe's Eurocodes increase design loads and reduce material strengths separately, rather than using one overall factor.
Safety factors are humility built into numbers.

cards.title: Voladizos
cards.text: Un voladizo está apoyado en un solo extremo: balcones, trampolines, escuadras de estantería. La parte superior está en tracción y la inferior en compresión, al revés que en una viga simplemente apoyada.

deep.x: A cantilever is supported at one end only and projects outward. It must resist both bending and the tendency to rotate.
Examples
Deflection
Cantilevers bend much more than beams supported at both ends. The tip deflection rises with the cube of the length.
Famous cantilevers
Cantilevers hang in the air by holding tight at one end.

cards.title: Columnas y pandeo
cards.text: Una columna alta y esbelta no se aplasta: primero pandea hacia un lado. Duplicar su longitud puede reducir su carga de pandeo a una cuarta parte; por eso las columnas se arriostran.

deep.x: Slender columns rarely fail by crushing. They buckle sideways suddenly at a load far below their crushing strength.

v.f: P crit = π² × E × I ÷ L²

deep.x: Length matters
Doubling the length cuts the buckling load to a quarter.
Bracing
Euler
Swiss mathematician Leonhard Euler derived the buckling formula in 1744.
Try it
Press down on a plastic ruler standing on end: it doesn't crush, it bows sideways.
Slender columns fail by buckling, not crushing.

cards.title: Láminas y cúpulas

items: Cáscara de huevo: fina pero fuerte
Cúpula del Panteón (Roma): hormigón sin armar

cards.text: Las láminas curvas reparten las cargas por su superficie, como la cáscara de un huevo. Las cúpulas, desde el Panteón de Roma hasta los estadios modernos, cubren espacios enormes con poco material.

deep.x: Curved shells carry loads through their surface, spreading forces efficiently. Thin shells can span large spaces with little material.
The Pantheon
Rome's Pantheon, completed around 125 AD, has a concrete dome 43 m across. It remains the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome, lightened by coffers and lighter aggregate higher up.
Why curves work
Modern examples
Curvature turns a thin surface into a strong one.

cards.title: Recorrido de cargas
cards.text: Toda carga debe bajar por la estructura hasta el suelo: del forjado a las vigas, de las vigas a los pilares, de los pilares a la cimentación. Si falta algún eslabón, algo falla.

deep.x: Every load must travel through the structure to the ground. Engineers trace a continuous load path for every force.
Missing links

items.w: Wall removed during renovation without checking
items.r: Engineer confirms whether it's load-bearing

deep.x: Hidden load paths
Removing a load-bearing wall, cutting a beam or overloading a balcony breaks the path. Loads then find another route, or the structure fails.
Wind and earthquake

items.b: wind and earthquakes, through bracing, walls and cores

deep.x: If you can't trace the load to the ground, something's missing.

cards.title: Cargas permanentes, variables y ambientales
cards.text: Los ingenieros diseñan para la carga permanente (el peso propio de la estructura), la carga variable (personas, muebles, nieve) y las cargas ambientales como el viento y los terremotos, y luego añaden factores de seguridad.

deep.x: Structures are designed for several kinds of loads, each with its own uncertainty and safety factor.
Typical floor loads
In Portugal
Portuguese buildings are designed to the Eurocodes, with special attention to seismic loads, especially in Lisbon, the Algarve and the Azores.
Load combinations
Engineers check combinations: dead plus live, dead plus wind, dead plus earthquake, with factors for each.
Structures must carry what they weigh, what we put on them, and what nature throws at them.

quiz.q: Una viga simplemente apoyada soporta una carga en el centro. ¿Dónde está en tracción?
quiz.explain: Se comba, así que la parte inferior se estira (tracción) y la superior se comprime (compresión).

quiz.q: ¿Por qué las celosías están hechas de triángulos?
options: Usan menos acero que los cuadrados
Un triángulo no puede deformarse sin que cambie la longitud de un lado
quiz.explain: Si los lados tienen longitud fija, los ángulos del triángulo quedan bloqueados, así que basta con uniones articuladas para que sea rígido.

quiz.q: Una cuerda con una carga de rotura de 600 kg se usa con un factor de seguridad de 5. ¿Carga de trabajo máxima?
quiz.explain: Carga de trabajo = carga de rotura ÷ FS = 600 ÷ 5 = 120 kg.

quiz.q: Un balcón sujeto solo a la pared es un…
quiz.explain: Está apoyado en un solo extremo.

quiz.q: ¿Qué suele hacer fallar a una columna alta y esbelta?
quiz.explain: Las columnas esbeltas pandean antes de aplastarse.

lessons.title: Materiales de ingeniería
lessons.summary: Acero, hormigón, madera, aluminio y plásticos.

cards.title: Resistencia y rigidez no son lo mismo
cards.text: La resistencia es cuánta tensión soporta un material antes de romperse o ceder. La rigidez es cuánto se resiste a doblarse o estirarse. El caucho es poco resistente y flexible; el vidrio es rígido pero frágil.

deep.x: Strength is how much stress a material withstands before failing. Stiffness is how much it resists deforming. A material can be strong but flexible, or stiff but weak.
Examples
Toughness
A third property, toughness, is the energy absorbed before fracture. Steel is tough; glass is not.
Design implications

x: Bridges must be stiff enough not to sway uncomfortably
Ropes must be strong but can stretch
Aircraft need strength and stiffness at low weight

deep.x: Strong, stiff and tough are three different virtues.

cards.title: Acero
cards.text: El acero es hierro con un poco de carbono. Resiste bien tanto la tracción como la compresión, es dúctil (se dobla antes de romperse) y reciclable, pero es pesado y se oxida si no se protege.

deep.x: Steel is iron with a small amount of carbon, usually under 2%. It's the backbone of modern construction and machinery.
Grades
Recycling
Steel is one of the most recycled materials in the world. Electric arc furnaces melt scrap with much lower emissions than making new steel from ore.
Production
Steel's ductility gives warning before failure.

cards.title: Hormigón
cards.text: El hormigón es cemento, agua, arena y grava. Es barato y muy resistente a la compresión, pero débil a la tracción, así que se añaden barras de acero (armaduras) donde aparece la tracción.

deep.x: Concrete is a mix of cement, water, sand and gravel. It's the world's most used construction material after water.
Strength
Tensile strength is only about a tenth of compressive strength.
Curing
Concrete hardens through a chemical reaction with water, not by drying. It gains most of its strength in about 28 days and must be kept moist while curing.
Prestressed concrete
Steel tendons are tensioned before or after casting, squeezing the concrete so it stays in compression even under load. It allows longer spans.
Concrete loves compression; steel handles the tension.

cards.title: Madera

l.t: En el sentido de la fibra

cards.text: La madera es resistente en el sentido de la fibra y débil en perpendicular. Para su peso es notablemente resistente, almacena carbono y es fácil de trabajar, pero hay que controlar la humedad, el fuego y los insectos.

deep.x: Wood is a natural composite of cellulose fibres in a lignin matrix. It's strong along the grain, light and renewable.
Strength for weight
Engineered timber
Modern timber buildings
Engineered timber now enables tall buildings: the Ascent tower in Milwaukee, completed in 2022, reaches about 87 m.
Challenges
Wood is a carbon store you can build with.

cards.title: Aluminio
cards.text: El aluminio pesa aproximadamente un tercio que el acero y no se oxida (una fina capa de óxido lo protege). Es menos rígido, así que las piezas se hacen más gruesas o con formas ingeniosas. Se usa en aviones, marcos de ventanas y coches.

deep.x: Aluminium is about a third the density of steel and naturally resists corrosion through a thin oxide layer.
Strengths and limits
Energy
Making new aluminium uses a lot of electricity. Recycling it uses about 5% of that energy, so recycled aluminium is highly valuable.
Uses
Light and corrosion-free, but less stiff than steel.

cards.title: Plásticos y materiales compuestos
cards.text: Los plásticos son ligeros, baratos y moldeables. Los materiales compuestos, como la fibra de carbono, integran fibras resistentes en una resina, lo que da una resistencia y una rigidez muy altas para su peso: bicis, aviones, coches de carreras.

deep.x: Plastics are light, cheap and easy to shape. Composites combine materials to get properties neither has alone.

items.b: melt and reshape: PE, PP, PVC, nylon
very stiff and strong for weight

deep.x: Composites
Uses

items: Aircraft (e.g. Boeing 787 about 50% composites by weight)

deep.x: Drawbacks
Composites put strong fibres exactly where the loads go.

cards.title: Elegir un material
cards.text: Los ingenieros sopesan resistencia, rigidez, peso, coste, durabilidad, facilidad de fabricación e impacto ambiental. Nunca hay un material perfecto, solo el mejor compromiso.

deep.x: Material selection balances many properties against cost and practicality. There's no perfect material, only the best compromise.
Ashby charts
Engineers use charts plotting properties against each other (like stiffness versus density) to find materials that best fit a requirement.
Example
Life-cycle thinking
The best material depends on what matters most for the job.

cards.title: Carbono incorporado
cards.text: Fabricar cemento libera mucho CO₂: alrededor del 8 % de las emisiones mundiales, según muchas estimaciones. La producción de acero también emite mucho carbono. Eso está impulsando el interés por los edificios de madera y los cementos bajos en carbono.

deep.x: Embodied carbon is the greenhouse gas emitted in making materials and building structures. Cement and steel are major sources.

items.l: global CO₂ from cement (widely cited estimate)

deep.x: Why cement emits
About half the emissions come from the chemistry itself, not the fuel.
Reductions
Design matters
Optimising structures to use less material can cut embodied carbon substantially at no extra cost.
The greenest material is the one you don't need to use.

cards.title: Corrosión
cards.text: El acero se oxida al exponerse al oxígeno y al agua, sobre todo con sal. Se protege con pintura, galvanizado (recubrimiento de zinc), aleaciones inoxidables y manteniendo un recubrimiento de hormigón sobre las armaduras.

deep.x: Corrosion is the gradual destruction of metals by chemical reaction with their environment. Rusting steel is the most familiar form.
What drives rust
Salt accelerates corrosion, which is why coastal and road-salted structures suffer most.
Rebar corrosion
Rusting steel expands inside concrete, cracking it from within (spalling). Adequate concrete cover and good quality concrete protect rebar.
Cost
Corrosion costs are estimated at around 3% of global GDP each year.
Keep water and salt away from steel, and it lasts.

cards.title: Vidrio
cards.text: El vidrio es muy resistente a la compresión pero frágil: un arañazo diminuto puede iniciar una grieta. El vidrio templado se trata con calor para ser mucho más resistente y se rompe en trocitos pequeños sin filo; el vidrio laminado se mantiene unido.

deep.x: Glass is stiff and strong in compression but brittle. Tiny surface flaws can start cracks that spread instantly.
Laminated glass
Two or more sheets bonded with a plastic interlayer stay together when broken. Car windscreens and glass floors use it.
Why glass is "weak"
In theory, glass is extremely strong. In practice, microscopic scratches concentrate stress and start cracks.
Uses
Tempered glass can't be cut after treatment; it must be shaped first.

quiz.q: ¿Por qué el hormigón armado lleva barras de acero?
options: El hormigón resiste mal la tracción, así que el acero soporta los esfuerzos de tracción
quiz.explain: Las armaduras absorben la tracción.

quiz.q: La madera es más resistente…
options: En el sentido de la fibra
quiz.explain: Las fibras van en el sentido de la veta.

quiz.q: ¿Cuál es el más ligero por volumen?
quiz.explain: El aluminio tiene aproximadamente un tercio de la densidad del acero.

lessons.title: Tensión y deformación
lessons.summary: Cómo se estiran, se doblan y se rompen los materiales.

cards.title: Tensión
example: 10 kN sobre una barra de acero de 100 mm²
cards.text: La tensión es la fuerza dividida por el área que la soporta. La misma fuerza sobre una barra más delgada crea más tensión. Unidades: pascales (N/m²), normalmente megapascales (MPa).

deep.x: Stress is force divided by the area carrying it. It tells you how hard the material is working, regardless of size.
Units
Example

x: 10 kN on a 10 mm diameter steel rod

deep.x: Types of stress
Stress shows how hard each square millimetre is working.

cards.title: Deformación
example: Una barra de 2 m se estira 1 mm
cards.text: La deformación es cuánto se estira un material en comparación con su longitud original. No tiene unidades y suele ser diminuta.

deep.x: Strain is the change in length divided by the original length. It's a ratio with no units, usually very small.
Example
Measuring strain
Strain gauges, thin foil patterns glued to a surface, change resistance as they stretch. They monitor bridges, aircraft and weighing scales.
Microstrain
Strain is stretch per unit length.

cards.title: Módulo de Young
cards.text: La rigidez se mide con el módulo de Young: la tensión dividida por la deformación. El acero ronda los 200 GPa, el aluminio unos 70 y la madera unos 10 en el sentido de la fibra.

deep.x: Young's modulus measures stiffness: how much stress is needed for a given strain in the elastic range.
What it means
Steel is about three times stiffer than aluminium. An aluminium part needs to be deeper or thicker to match a steel part's stiffness.
History
Named after English scientist Thomas Young, who described it in 1807, though similar ideas were explored earlier.
Hooke's law

items.m: Springs stretch in proportion to force

deep.x: Young's modulus is a material's stiffness, independent of shape.

cards.title: Elástico y plástico
cards.text: En el rango elástico, un material recupera su forma al descargarlo. Pasado el límite elástico se deforma de manera permanente (plástico). Los ingenieros diseñan las estructuras para que sigan en el rango elástico en uso normal.

deep.x: In the elastic range, materials spring back fully when unloaded. Beyond the yield point, they deform permanently.
Everyday examples
Design principle
Structures are designed to stay elastic under normal loads. Plastic behaviour provides a reserve in extreme events, like earthquakes.
Elastic means it returns; plastic means it remembers.

cards.title: La curva tensión–deformación
cards.text: Ensayar una barra de acero en una máquina dibuja una curva: una recta elástica, un límite elástico, luego un estiramiento plástico hasta la resistencia última y, por último, la rotura.

deep.x: Tensile testing pulls a sample until it breaks, recording a stress-strain curve that reveals key properties.
Key values from the curve
Necking
After the ultimate strength, the bar narrows locally ("necks"), and the force needed drops until fracture.
Typical structural steel
One test reveals stiffness, strength and ductility.

cards.title: Dúctil frente a frágil
cards.text: Los materiales dúctiles (acero, cobre) se estiran mucho antes de romperse, lo que sirve de aviso. Los frágiles (vidrio, fundición, hormigón) se rompen de golpe. La ductilidad hace más seguras las estructuras.

deep.x: Ductile materials stretch and bend significantly before breaking. Brittle materials fracture suddenly with little deformation.
Why ductility matters
A ductile structure bends and sags before collapsing, giving people time to escape and engineers warning signs.
Temperature effects
Some steels become brittle in extreme cold. The Liberty ships of World War II suffered brittle fractures in cold seas, prompting new research into steel toughness.
Earthquake design
Seismic codes require ductile detailing: steel reinforcement arranged so concrete members bend without sudden collapse.
Ductility is a material's way of warning you.

cards.title: Tensión de flexión
cards.text: Cuando una viga se flexiona, la tensión es cero en el centro (eje neutro) y máxima en las superficies superior e inferior. Por eso las vigas en I colocan el material lejos del centro.

deep.x: When a beam bends, stress varies across its depth: zero at the neutral axis, maximum at the top and bottom surfaces.
Stress distribution
Consequences

items: I-beams put material at top and bottom
Holes near the neutral axis do little harm

deep.x: Maximum moment

x: Simply supported beam, central load P, span L

deep.x: Bending works the surfaces hardest.

cards.title: Momento de inercia
cards.text: La resistencia de una viga a la flexión depende muchísimo de su canto. En un rectángulo, duplicar el canto lo hace ocho veces más rígido. Por eso las viguetas se colocan de canto.

deep.x: The second moment of area (I) describes how a cross-section's shape resists bending. Depth matters enormously.
Depth vs width

v.unit: relative stiffness of a rectangular section

deep.x: Why joists stand on edge
Practical lessons

x: Deeper beams are much stiffer for the same material
Shelves sag less if they have a deep front lip
Ruler: easy to bend flat, very hard on edge

deep.x: Depth is cubed: double it and stiffness rises eightfold.

cards.title: Dilatación térmica
cards.text: Los materiales crecen al calentarse. Un puente de acero de 100 m puede alargarse unos 4 cm entre el invierno y el verano, por eso tiene juntas de dilatación. Los raíles, las tuberías y las losas de hormigón también necesitan espacio para moverse.

deep.x: Materials expand when heated and contract when cooled. Structures must accommodate this movement.
Example
Coefficients
Solutions

items: Gaps in rails (or welded, stressed rails)
Movement joints in slabs and tiles

deep.x: Mixing materials
Steel and concrete expand at almost the same rate, one reason reinforced concrete works so well.
Leave room to grow: materials move with temperature.

cards.title: Concentraciones de tensión

items.w: esquina interior viva
items.r: acuerdo redondeado

items.w: ventana cuadrada en cabina presurizada
items.r: ventana redondeada

cards.text: Las esquinas vivas, los agujeros y las entallas concentran la tensión, a veces hasta el triple de la media. Las esquinas redondeadas (acuerdos) la reparten. Por eso las ventanillas de los aviones son redondeadas.

deep.x: Holes, notches and sharp corners concentrate stress locally, sometimes to several times the average. Cracks start there.

items.w: Sharp internal corner in a loaded part
items.r: Rounded fillet spreads the stress

deep.x: Stress concentration factor
The Comet disasters

In 1954, two de Havilland Comet jet airliners broke up in flight. Investigations traced fatigue cracks to sharp corners of openings in the pressurised fuselage. Since then, aircraft openings and windows have rounded corners.
Design practice
Sharp corners are where cracks are born.

quiz.q: 20 kN sobre una barra de 400 mm² producen una tensión de…
Poner un tablón de canto lo hace mucho más rígido porque…
options: La rigidez a flexión crece con el cubo del canto
A la madera le gusta estar vertical
quiz.explain: I = b × h³ ÷ 12.

quiz.q: ¿Qué material avisa antes de romperse?
quiz.explain: El acero dúctil se estira primero.

lessons.title: Rozamiento
lessons.summary: La fuerza que agarra, frena y desgasta las cosas.

cards.title: Qué es el rozamiento
cards.text: El rozamiento se opone al deslizamiento entre superficies. A escala microscópica, incluso las superficies lisas son rugosas, y sus salientes se enganchan y se adhieren brevemente.

deep.x: Friction resists sliding between surfaces. At the microscopic level, even polished surfaces are rough, touching only at tiny high points.
Classic laws

items.b: kinetic friction roughly independent of speed

deep.x: Leonardo first
Leonardo da Vinci studied friction around 1500, two centuries before Amontons, but his notes weren't published.
Energy
Friction turns motion into heat. Rub your hands together and feel it.
Friction is countless microscopic contacts resisting motion.

cards.title: Coeficiente de rozamiento
cards.text: La fuerza de rozamiento es aproximadamente la fuerza normal (lo fuerte que se aprietan las superficies) por un coeficiente μ que depende de los materiales.

deep.x: The friction force is roughly the normal force multiplied by a coefficient (μ) that depends on the two materials.
Example

x: 1,000 N box on wood floor, μ ≈ 0.4

deep.x: Variability
Coefficients vary with surface condition, moisture, temperature and contamination. Engineers use conservative values.
Friction depends on the pair of materials and how hard they press.

cards.title: Estático frente a dinámico
cards.text: Cuesta más fuerza hacer que algo empiece a deslizarse que mantenerlo en marcha. El rozamiento estático es mayor que el dinámico (de deslizamiento). Por eso el ABS evita que las ruedas se bloqueen.

deep.x: It takes more force to start sliding than to keep sliding. Static friction is generally higher than kinetic friction.
ABS brakes
A rolling tyre uses static friction at the contact patch; a locked, sliding tyre uses lower kinetic friction and can't steer.
Stick-slip
Alternating sticking and slipping causes squeaky doors, creaking floors and violin sounds.
Once it starts sliding, it's easier to keep it sliding.

cards.title: Frenos

steps: La energía cinética se vuelve calor

cards.text: Los frenos convierten el movimiento en calor mediante el rozamiento entre pastillas y discos. En una bajada larga, los frenos pueden sobrecalentarse y perder eficacia; usar el freno motor o la regeneración de un coche eléctrico ayuda.

deep.x: Brakes convert kinetic energy into heat through friction between pads and discs or drums.
Energy involved

x: All turned to heat in a stop

deep.x: Brake fade
On long descents, brakes overheat and friction drops. Using lower gears (engine braking) or EV regenerative braking prevents fade.
Brake types
Brake dust
Brake wear releases fine particles, a significant source of urban air pollution. EVs produce less because they brake mostly by regeneration.
Brakes turn speed into heat.

cards.title: Neumáticos y agarre
cards.text: Los neumáticos agarran gracias al rozamiento y a una ligera deformación de la goma. Con la carretera mojada, los surcos del dibujo evacuan el agua; sin ellos, el neumático puede hacer aquaplaning sobre una película de agua.

deep.x: Tyres grip the road through friction and the rubber's slight deformation into the road surface texture.
Aquaplaning
Tread depth
Stopping distances

v.unit: stopping distance from 80 km/h in wet, m (illustrative)

deep.x: Pressure
Under-inflated tyres overheat, wear unevenly, increase fuel use and reduce grip.
Tyres are the only contact between car and road: about four postcards' worth.

cards.title: Lubricación
cards.text: El aceite y la grasa separan las superficies con una película fina, lo que reduce drásticamente el rozamiento y el desgaste. Los motores, los rodamientos y las cajas de cambios dependen de ella.

deep.x: Lubricants separate surfaces with a thin film, dramatically reducing friction and wear.
Lubrication regimes
Types
Engine oil
Engine oil lubricates, cools, cleans and protects against corrosion. Changing it at recommended intervals prevents expensive wear.
A film thinner than a hair separates metal from metal.

cards.title: Rodamientos
cards.text: Los rodamientos de bolas y de rodillos sustituyen el deslizamiento por la rodadura, que tiene mucho menos rozamiento. Están en ruedas, motores, ventiladores y discos duros.

deep.x: Bearings support rotating shafts with minimal friction. Rolling bearings replace sliding with rolling.
Types
Where they are
Failure signs
Rolling beats sliding by a factor of a hundred.

cards.title: Rozamiento útil
cards.text: Sin rozamiento no podrías andar, conducir, sujetar un bolígrafo ni mantener una tuerca en un tornillo. Los ingenieros a menudo añaden rozamiento a propósito: discos de embrague, transmisiones por correa, suelos antideslizantes.

deep.x: Friction isn't just an enemy. Much of daily life depends on it, and engineers often add it on purpose.
Engineered friction
Friction in fasteners
Bolted joints hold mainly through friction between clamped surfaces, created by bolt tension. That's why correct torque matters.
Without friction
Imagine walking on perfectly frictionless ice: you couldn't start, stop or turn.
Friction holds the world together.

cards.title: Resistencia a la rodadura
cards.text: Incluso al rodar, los neumáticos pierden energía porque la goma se flexiona. Los neumáticos de baja resistencia a la rodadura y la presión correcta ahorran combustible o autonomía eléctrica.

deep.x: Rolling tyres lose energy because rubber flexes and recovers with each rotation. This rolling resistance affects fuel use and EV range.
Why trains are efficient
Steel wheels on steel rails deform very little, giving rolling resistance about a tenth of car tyres.
Saving energy
EU tyre label
EU tyre labels rate rolling resistance (energy efficiency), wet grip and noise, helping buyers compare.
Pump up your tyres: it's free efficiency.

cards.title: El coste del desgaste

items.l: de la energía mundial se usa para vencer el rozamiento (estimación)

cards.text: Según estudios de tribología, se estima que el rozamiento y el desgaste consumen alrededor de una quinta parte de la energía mundial y causan grandes pérdidas por piezas desgastadas. Mejores lubricantes y materiales ahorran mucho.

deep.x: Friction and wear consume a large share of the world's energy and cause huge losses through worn components.

items.l: world energy used to overcome friction (estimate)
the science of friction, wear and lubrication

deep.x: Where energy goes
Savings potential
Studies by tribologists such as Kenneth Holmberg and Ali Erdemir suggest new technologies could cut friction losses significantly over decades.
Solutions
Reducing friction is one of the quietest ways to save energy.

quiz.q: ¿Qué fuerza necesita aproximadamente una caja de 50 kg (≈490 N) sobre un suelo con μ = 0,4 para deslizarse?
¿Por qué cuesta más empezar a empujar una caja que mantenerla en movimiento?
options: El rozamiento estático es mayor que el dinámico
quiz.explain: Para arrancar hay que vencer el rozamiento estático.

quiz.q: ¿Qué hacen los rodamientos de bolas?
options: Sustituyen el deslizamiento por una rodadura de bajo rozamiento
quiz.explain: Rodar ofrece mucha menos resistencia que deslizar.

lessons.title: Trabajo, energía y potencia
lessons.summary: Levantar, mover y la rapidez con que ocurre.

cards.title: Trabajo
cards.text: Se realiza trabajo cuando una fuerza mueve algo: fuerza por distancia. Sube una bolsa de 10 kg 1 m y harás unos 98 J de trabajo.

deep.x: In physics, work is done when a force moves something in the direction of the force. It's measured in joules.

items.m: distance moved in the force's direction

deep.x: Example
No movement, no work
Holding a heavy bag still does no physical work, even though your muscles tire. Your muscles use energy to stay tense, but nothing moves.
Everyday work
Work is force multiplied by distance moved.

cards.title: Energía potencial
example: 1 tonelada de agua que cae 100 m
cards.text: Elevar algo almacena energía que se libera cuando cae. Las presas hidroeléctricas lo aprovechan con millones de toneladas de agua.

deep.x: Raising an object against gravity stores gravitational potential energy, which can be released when it falls.
Example
Hydroelectric power
Pumped storage
Portugal's pumped-storage plants pump water uphill when electricity is cheap and release it when needed, storing energy as height.
Other forms

items: Raised weights in gravity storage systems

deep.x: Height is stored energy.

cards.title: Energía cinética
example: Coche de 1500 kg a 50 km/h frente a 100 km/h
cards.text: Los objetos en movimiento llevan una energía que crece con el cuadrado de la velocidad. Si duplicas la velocidad, la energía se multiplica por cuatro; por eso la velocidad importa tanto en los choques.

deep.x: Moving objects carry kinetic energy, which grows with the square of speed.
Speed matters most

v.unit: kinetic energy of a 1,500 kg car, kJ

deep.x: In crashes
Doubling speed quadruples the energy a crash must absorb. Going from 50 to 70 km/h nearly doubles crash energy.
Braking distance
Braking distance also rises with the square of speed, because brakes must remove all that energy.
Double the speed, four times the energy.

cards.title: Potencia
cards.text: La potencia es la rapidez con que se realiza un trabajo: julios por segundo, o vatios. Un ciclista fuerte mantiene unos 200–300 W; el motor de un coche da de decenas a cientos de kW.

deep.x: Power is the rate of doing work or using energy, measured in watts: joules per second.
Peak vs sustained
Climbing stairs
Power is how fast the work gets done.

cards.title: Caballos de potencia
cards.text: James Watt definió el caballo de potencia para vender máquinas de vapor: unos 746 W en la versión imperial. El caballo de vapor métrico (CV en España, cv en Portugal) equivale a unos 735 W.

deep.x: James Watt defined the horsepower in the 1780s to compare his steam engines with the draft horses they replaced.
Converting
Was it realistic?
Watt estimated a horse could sustain about 33,000 foot-pounds per minute. Real horses can produce more in short bursts but less over a full day.
Car specs in Portugal
Portuguese car advertisements often quote power in cv, while technical documents use kW. EU documents require kW.
One horsepower is about three-quarters of a kilowatt.

cards.title: Rendimiento
cards.text: Ninguna máquina convierte toda la energía de entrada en energía útil; parte se convierte en calor o ruido. El rendimiento es la energía útil dividida por la de entrada.

deep.x: No machine converts all input energy into useful output. Efficiency is the useful output divided by the input.

items.m: The rest becomes heat, noise, vibration

deep.x: Where losses go
Chains of efficiency
Every conversion loses something; fewer conversions lose less.

cards.title: La energía se conserva

steps: El rozamiento convierte parte en calor

cards.text: La energía cambia de forma, pero el total sigue siendo el mismo. Una montaña rusa que cae convierte energía potencial en cinética y luego al revés, menos las pérdidas por rozamiento.

deep.x: Energy can't be created or destroyed, only converted from one form to another. The total always stays the same.

steps: Friction slowly turns it to heat

deep.x: Roller coasters
A roller coaster's first hill is the tallest because no later hill can be higher: friction has already turned some energy into heat.
Forms of energy
Perpetual motion

items.w: A machine that runs forever with no energy input
items.r: Impossible: friction always turns some energy into heat

deep.x: Energy changes form but never disappears.

cards.title: Julios y kWh
cards.text: Los ingenieros usan julios; las facturas de la luz, kWh. Un kWh son 3,6 millones de julios, la energía de una estufa de 1 kW funcionando una hora.

deep.x: Engineers and scientists measure energy in joules; electricity bills use kilowatt-hours. Converting between them is simple.
Everyday energy
Food vs electricity
A human runs on roughly the energy of a 100 W bulb.
3.6 million joules make one kilowatt-hour.

cards.title: La energía de los combustibles
cards.text: Un litro de gasolina contiene unos 9 kWh de energía química; por eso costaba tanto superar a los combustibles líquidos. Las baterías de litio almacenan mucho menos por kilo, pero los sistemas de propulsión eléctricos aprovechan la energía de forma mucho más eficiente.

deep.x: Liquid fuels pack a lot of energy into a small volume, which is why they dominated transport for a century.
Why EVs still compete
Per litre
Hydrogen
Hydrogen has huge energy per kilo but very little per litre unless compressed or liquefied, making storage hard.
Fuel stores lots of energy; electric motors waste less of it.

cards.title: Muelles
cards.text: Un muelle almacena energía cuando se estira o se comprime. Su fuerza es proporcional a lo que se desplaza (ley de Hooke), y se usa en suspensiones, básculas y relojes.

deep.x: Springs store energy when stretched or compressed. Within their elastic range, force is proportional to deflection.

v.f: F = k × x; Energy = ½ × k × x²

deep.x: Uses
Example

x: Spring with k = 10,000 N/m compressed 5 cm

deep.x: Fatigue
Springs that flex millions of times can fail by fatigue. Valve springs in engines are designed for billions of cycles.
Robert Hooke published his law in 1678 as a Latin anagram, "ceiiinosssttuv", standing for "ut tensio, sic vis": as the extension, so the force.

quiz.q: La energía cinética a 100 km/h comparada con la de 50 km/h es…
quiz.explain: La energía crece con el cuadrado de la velocidad.

quiz.q: ¿Cuánto trabajo supone aproximadamente levantar 20 kg a 2 m de altura?
1 kWh equivale a…

lessons.title: Fluidos e hidráulica
lessons.summary: Presión, flotación y la fuerza de los líquidos.

cards.title: Presión
cards.text: La presión es una fuerza repartida sobre un área. Un tacón de aguja aprieta el suelo mucho más que la pata de un elefante, porque el área es diminuta.

deep.x: Pressure is force spread over an area. The same force concentrated on a small area produces huge pressure.
Heel vs elephant
Units
Applications
Spread force to reduce pressure; concentrate it to cut.

cards.title: La presión en el agua
cards.text: La presión del agua aumenta con la profundidad, alrededor de 1 bar cada 10 metros. Los buceadores la notan en los oídos; las presas son más gruesas en la base por el mismo motivo.

deep.x: Water pressure increases steadily with depth, because of the weight of water above.
Roughly 1 bar per 10 m
Dams
Dams are thicker at the bottom, where water pressure is greatest. Large concrete dams can be many times thicker at the base than at the crest.
Divers
Divers equalise ear pressure as they descend. Every 10 m adds about one atmosphere.
Water towers

steps: Taps below get pressure without pumps running

deep.x: Every 10 metres of water adds one bar.

cards.title: Presión atmosférica
cards.text: El aire que tenemos encima empuja hacia abajo con alrededor de 1 bar (101 kPa) al nivel del mar, unas 10 toneladas por cada metro cuadrado. No lo notamos porque empuja por igual desde todos los lados.

deep.x: The weight of the air above us creates atmospheric pressure, about 1 bar at sea level.
Why we don't notice
Pressure acts equally in all directions, and our bodies contain fluids at the same pressure, so forces balance.
The Magdeburg hemispheres
In 1654, Otto von Guericke pumped the air out of two joined copper hemispheres. Teams of horses couldn't pull them apart: atmospheric pressure held them together.
With altitude
We live at the bottom of an ocean of air.

cards.title: El principio de Pascal
example: 100 N sobre 1 cm², salida de 50 cm²
cards.text: La presión en un líquido cerrado se transmite por igual en todas las direcciones. Empuja un pistón pequeño y un pistón grande recibe la misma presión sobre un área mayor, lo que da una fuerza mayor.

deep.x: Pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally throughout. A small force on a small piston creates a large force on a large piston.
Example

x: Small piston 1 cm², big piston 100 cm²

deep.x: The trade-off
The small piston must move 100 times farther than the large one rises. Energy is conserved.
History
Blaise Pascal described the principle in the 1650s. Joseph Bramah patented the hydraulic press in 1795.
Fluids are nearly incompressible

items: air in brake lines is dangerous

deep.x: Pressure travels; area multiplies force.

cards.title: La hidráulica está en todas partes
cards.text: Los frenos de los coches, las excavadoras, los elevadores y las prensas usan fluido hidráulico para multiplicar la fuerza y transmitirla por mangueras flexibles.

deep.x: Hydraulic systems multiply and transmit force through fluid in hoses and cylinders. They're compact, powerful and controllable.
Car brakes
Why hydraulics
Brake fluid
Brake fluid absorbs moisture over time, lowering its boiling point. That's why it should be replaced every couple of years.
Hydraulics put enormous force at the end of a flexible hose.

cards.title: Flotación
cards.text: Un objeto dentro de un fluido recibe un empuje hacia arriba igual al peso del fluido que desplaza (Arquímedes). Si es mayor que su propio peso, flota. Los barcos de acero flotan porque su forma desplaza mucha agua.

deep.x: Archimedes' principle: an object in a fluid is pushed up by a force equal to the weight of fluid it displaces.
Why steel ships float
A steel ship's hollow shape displaces a large volume of water, whose weight equals the ship's weight before the hull is fully submerged.
Density decides

items.b: floats in salt water more easily

deep.x: Submarines
Submarines flood or empty ballast tanks to change their average density, letting them dive or surface.
According to legend, Archimedes shouted "Eureka!" when he realised in his bath how to test whether a king's crown was pure gold.

cards.title: Flujo en tuberías
cards.text: El caudal es la velocidad por el área de la tubería. Aprieta una manguera y el agua sale más rápido. Las tuberías estrechas necesitan más presión para mover el mismo caudal debido al rozamiento.

deep.x: The flow rate of a fluid is its speed multiplied by the pipe's cross-section. In a narrower section, the fluid speeds up.
Squeeze the hose
Friction losses
Friction losses rise steeply with speed, so undersized pipes waste pumping energy.
Home plumbing
Same flow through a smaller pipe means faster water and more friction.

cards.title: Bernoulli
cards.text: Donde un fluido se mueve más rápido, su presión baja. Esto ayuda a explicar los carburadores, los atomizadores y parte de cómo las alas y las velas generan sustentación.

deep.x: Bernoulli's principle, published by Daniel Bernoulli in 1738, says that where a fluid flows faster, its pressure is lower (along a streamline).
Examples
Venturi tube

steps: Narrow throat: speed rises, pressure falls

deep.x: Lift and Bernoulli
Bernoulli's principle helps explain the pressure difference on wings, but popular "equal transit time" explanations are wrong. Lift is best understood as the wing deflecting air downward.
Faster flow, lower pressure.

cards.title: Sifones

steps: La gravedad tira del lado largo

cards.text: Un sifón hace subir un líquido por encima de un obstáculo y bajarlo hasta un punto más bajo sin bomba, siempre que la salida esté por debajo del origen y el tubo empiece lleno.

deep.x: A siphon moves liquid from a higher container to a lower one, over a barrier, without a pump, once the tube is filled.
Limits

items.b: about 10 m for water at sea level

deep.x: Uses
How it works
Gravity pulling liquid down the longer leg, together with atmospheric pressure and the liquid's cohesion, keeps the flow going.
Fill the tube, keep the outlet low, and gravity does the pumping.

cards.title: Viscosidad
cards.text: La viscosidad es lo espeso que es un fluido: la miel es viscosa, el agua no. Los grados de aceite como 5W-30 describen cómo se comporta la viscosidad en frío (5W) y en caliente (30).

deep.x: Viscosity is a fluid's resistance to flow: its "thickness". Honey is highly viscous; water isn't.

v.unit: approx. viscosity, mPa·s at room temperature

deep.x: Temperature
Most liquids become thinner when hot and thicker when cold. Engine oil must flow when cold and still protect when hot.
Oil grades
Non-Newtonian fluids
Viscosity is how much a fluid resists flowing.

quiz.q: ¿Cuánto aumenta aproximadamente la presión por cada 10 m de profundidad en el agua?
quiz.explain: Alrededor de 1 bar cada 10 m.

quiz.q: Un gato hidráulico con una relación de áreas de 20 convierte 50 N en…
¿Por qué flota un barco de acero?
options: Su forma desplaza un peso de agua mayor que el suyo propio
El aire lo empuja hacia arriba
quiz.explain: El principio de Arquímedes.

lessons.title: Cómo vuelan los aviones
lessons.summary: Sustentación, resistencia, empuje y peso.

cards.title: Cuatro fuerzas
cards.text: En vuelo estable, la sustentación equilibra el peso y el empuje equilibra la resistencia. Para subir, la sustentación supera al peso; para acelerar, el empuje supera a la resistencia.

deep.x: In flight, four forces act on an aircraft: lift, weight, thrust and drag.
Steady flight
In level flight at constant speed, lift equals weight and thrust equals drag. The plane isn't "pushing harder" than in cruise; forces are balanced.
Manoeuvres
Weight changes
Airliners burn tens of tonnes of fuel on long flights, getting lighter and able to climb to higher, more efficient altitudes.
Steady flight is a balance of four forces.

cards.title: Cómo generan sustentación las alas
cards.text: Un ala tiene una forma y una inclinación (ángulo de ataque) que desvían el aire hacia abajo. Empujar el aire hacia abajo empuja el ala hacia arriba (tercera ley de Newton), con menos presión por encima del ala y más por debajo.

deep.x: A wing creates lift by deflecting air downward. By Newton's third law, pushing air down pushes the wing up.
Two views, one phenomenon
Both describe the same physics.
A myth

items.w: Air over the top must meet the air underneath at the trailing edge
items.r: Air over the top actually arrives sooner, equal transit time is false

deep.x: Angle of attack
Even a flat plate generates lift at an angle. The curved shape (camber) makes wings more efficient and gentler at stalling.
Wings fly by pushing air down.

cards.title: La ecuación de la sustentación

viz.f: L = ½ × ρ × v² × S × CL

cards.text: La sustentación crece con la densidad del aire, la superficie alar y el cuadrado de la velocidad. Por eso los aviones necesitan pistas largas en aeropuertos altos y calurosos, donde el aire está enrarecido.

deep.x: Lift depends on air density, speed, wing area and a lift coefficient set by wing shape and angle of attack.

v.f: L = ½ × ρ × v² × S × CL

deep.x: Speed squared
Hot and high
Hot air and high altitudes mean thinner air. Planes need higher speeds and longer runways to take off from airports such as Mexico City or La Paz.
Weight limits
On hot days at high-altitude airports, airlines sometimes reduce passengers, cargo or fuel to take off safely.
Thin air demands more speed for the same lift.

cards.title: Pérdida
cards.text: Si aumentas demasiado el ángulo de ataque, el flujo de aire se separa de la superficie superior. La sustentación se desploma de repente: es la entrada en pérdida. Los pilotos entrenan para reconocerla y recuperarse.

deep.x: A stall occurs when the wing's angle of attack is too high. Airflow separates from the upper surface and lift drops sharply.
Stall isn't engine failure

items.w: "The engine stalled, so the plane fell"
items.r: An aerodynamic stall is about wing angle, not engines

deep.x: Recovery
Warnings
Aircraft have stall warning systems: horns, stick shakers and, in modern airliners, protections that limit angle of attack.
Air France 447
In 2009, Air France flight 447 crashed into the Atlantic after the crew failed to recognise and recover from a high-altitude stall, a tragedy that reshaped pilot training.
Stall depends on angle, not speed alone.

cards.title: Flaps y slats
cards.text: Para el despegue y el aterrizaje, los flaps y los slats se extienden desde el ala para aumentar su superficie y su curvatura, lo que da más sustentación a baja velocidad.

deep.x: Flaps and slats change a wing's shape for slow flight, allowing take-off and landing at lower speeds.
How they help

items.b: extend from trailing edge, increase area and camber
extend from leading edge, delay stall
reduce lift and add drag after landing

deep.x: Landing speeds
Watch from the window
Next time you fly, watch the wing transform before landing: slats move forward, flaps slide back and down, and spoilers pop up on touchdown.
Flaps let a fast wing fly slowly.

cards.title: Resistencia aerodinámica
cards.text: La resistencia procede del rozamiento con el aire y de la diferencia de presión detrás del objeto. Crece con el cuadrado de la velocidad, así que ir más rápido cuesta mucho más combustible.

deep.x: Drag resists motion through air. It rises with the square of speed, so faster travel costs disproportionately more energy.

v.f: D = ½ × ρ × v² × S × CD

deep.x: Types of drag
Power needed
Power to overcome drag rises with the cube of speed: cycling at 30 km/h takes far more effort than at 20 km/h.
Winglets
Upturned wingtips reduce induced drag, saving several percent of fuel on airliners.
Speed costs: drag squares it, power cubes it.

cards.title: Motores a reacción

steps: La turbina y la tobera empujan el avión

cards.text: Un turbofán aspira aire, lo comprime, quema combustible en él y expulsa el gas caliente por detrás. En los aviones de pasajeros, la mayor parte del empuje viene del gran ventilador que impulsa el aire alrededor del núcleo.

deep.x: Modern airliners use turbofan engines: a large fan pushes most air around the engine core, providing most of the thrust efficiently.

steps: Some air to core: compressed, burned, expanded

deep.x: Bypass ratio
Why big fans
Accelerating a lot of air gently is more efficient than accelerating a little air violently. That's why modern engines have huge fans.
Temperatures
Turbine blades operate in gas hotter than their melting point, protected by cooling air channels and special coatings.
Most of a modern jet's thrust comes from its fan.

cards.title: Por qué los aviones vuelan tan alto
cards.text: A unos 10–12 km de altitud el aire está enrarecido, así que la resistencia es mucho menor y los motores a reacción son más eficientes. Las cabinas se presurizan al equivalente de unos 2000 m.

deep.x: At 10–12 km altitude, thin air reduces drag, and jet engines run efficiently. Most weather is also below.
Cabin pressure
Cabins are pressurised to the equivalent of about 1,800–2,400 m altitude. Newer composite aircraft like the Boeing 787 use lower cabin altitudes and higher humidity for comfort.
Above the weather

items: Jet streams can speed up eastbound flights

deep.x: Contrails
Contrails form when hot, humid exhaust meets cold air and water freezes into ice crystals. Their climate effect is an active research area.
High altitude means thin air, low drag and efficient engines.

cards.title: Superficies de mando
cards.text: Los alerones de las alas hacen alabear el avión, el timón de profundidad de la cola lo hace cabecear arriba y abajo, y el timón de dirección lo hace guiñar a izquierda y derecha.

deep.x: Pilots control an aircraft's attitude around three axes using movable surfaces.

items.b: on wings, roll left and right
on tail, pitch nose up and down
on fin, yaw nose left and right

deep.x: Coordinated turns
Fly-by-wire
Modern airliners use fly-by-wire: pilot inputs go to computers, which move control surfaces and protect against dangerous manoeuvres.
Trim
Trim tabs adjust surfaces so the plane flies steadily without constant pilot force.
Roll, pitch and yaw: three axes, three controls.

cards.title: Drones
cards.text: Los drones multirrotor no tienen alas; generan sustentación haciendo girar hélices. Se dirigen acelerando unos motores y frenando otros, con una controladora de vuelo que hace ajustes cientos de veces por segundo.

deep.x: Multirotor drones fly without wings, using spinning propellers for lift and changing their speeds to steer.
Control by speed differences
Sensors
Efficiency
Rules
EU drone rules require registration of operators for most drones with cameras, and limit flights near people and airports.
Drones steer by changing motor speeds hundreds of times a second.

quiz.q: ¿Qué ocurre en una pérdida?
options: El flujo de aire se separa del ala y la sustentación cae bruscamente
quiz.explain: Un ángulo de ataque demasiado alto.

quiz.q: Duplicar la velocidad multiplica la resistencia por un factor de aproximadamente…
quiz.explain: La resistencia crece con el cuadrado de la velocidad.

quiz.q: ¿Qué superficie de mando hace alabear el avión?
quiz.explain: Los alerones se mueven en sentidos opuestos en cada ala.

lessons.title: Puentes
lessons.summary: De viga, de arco, colgantes y atirantados.

cards.title: Los principales tipos de puente
cards.text: Los puentes soportan las cargas de forma distinta: las vigas se flexionan, los arcos se comprimen, los cables de los puentes colgantes tiran, y las torres de los atirantados sostienen el tablero con cables rectos.

deep.x: Bridge types differ in how they carry loads to the ground: by bending, compression or tension.
Typical spans
Choosing
Record holders
The world's longest suspension span, the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge in Turkey (2022), spans just over 2 km.
Each bridge type uses a different force to cross the gap.

cards.title: Puentes de viga
cards.text: El puente más sencillo: una viga sobre apoyos. Barato y rápido para luces cortas, pero a medida que crece la luz hacen falta vigas de mucho canto, así que a menudo son continuos sobre muchas pilas.

deep.x: A beam bridge is a horizontal beam resting on supports. It's the simplest and most common bridge type.
Limits
As spans grow, beams must get much deeper to stay stiff, adding weight. Beyond a few hundred metres, other types are more efficient.
Viaducts
Long viaducts are often chains of beam spans on many piers, like motorway viaducts across valleys.
Construction
Beam bridges are simple, cheap and everywhere.

cards.title: Puentes de arco
cards.text: Los arcos llevan las cargas a compresión hasta estribos sólidos. Hay arcos de piedra que han durado 2000 años. El puente Dom Luís I de Oporto (1886) es un arco de hierro de dos tableros sobre el Duero.

deep.x: Arch bridges carry loads in compression to strong abutments. Stone arches have lasted for millennia.
Porto's arches

items.b: 1877, iron railway arch by Eiffel's company
1886, double-deck iron arch by Théophile Seyrig

deep.x: Arrábida
When it opened in 1963, Edgar Cardoso's Arrábida Bridge had the longest reinforced concrete arch span in the world, about 270 m.
Roman legacy
The Pont du Gard aqueduct in France and Portugal's Roman bridges, like the one at Chaves, still stand after nearly 2,000 years.
Porto's bridges are a museum of arch engineering.

cards.title: Puentes colgantes
cards.text: Los cables principales cuelgan de torres altas y se anclan en cada extremo; unas péndolas verticales sostienen el tablero. Son los que alcanzan las mayores luces. El puente 25 de Abril de Lisboa (1966) es uno de ellos.

deep.x: Suspension bridges hang their decks from cables draped over towers and anchored at both ends. They achieve the longest spans.

steps: Anchorages in rock or massive blocks

deep.x: Lisbon's 25 de Abril Bridge
When it opened, it had the longest suspension span outside the United States.
Cable construction
Main cables are spun from thousands of parallel steel wires, compacted and wrapped. Each wire is only about 5 mm thick.
Flexibility
Suspension bridges move noticeably in wind and under traffic; this is normal and designed for.
Suspension bridges hang the road from cables in tension.

cards.title: Puentes atirantados
cards.text: Cables rectos van directamente de las torres al tablero en forma de abanico o de arpa. Son eficientes para luces medias y largas y rápidos de construir. El puente Vasco da Gama de Lisboa tiene un vano principal atirantado.

deep.x: Cable-stayed bridges support the deck with straight cables running directly from towers. They're efficient for medium to long spans.
Patterns
Vasco da Gama Bridge
It was among the longest bridges in Europe when built, crossing the Tagus estuary.
Popularity
Cable-stayed bridges have become the most popular choice for spans between about 200 and 1,000 m.
Straight cables, simple towers, efficient spans.

cards.title: Puentes portugueses
cards.text: Portugal tiene algunos puentes extraordinarios, entre ellos varios de la empresa de Gustave Eiffel y de Edgar Cardoso.

deep.x: Portugal has a rich bridge heritage, from Roman stone to record-breaking modern spans.
Edgar Cardoso
Engineer Edgar Cardoso (1913–2000) designed many notable Portuguese bridges, including the Arrábida and Edgar Cardoso bridges, and pioneered structural model testing.
Eiffel's connection
Infante D. Henrique Bridge
Porto's Infante D. Henrique Bridge (2003), designed by Adão da Fonseca, has a remarkably shallow concrete arch spanning about 280 m beneath a stiff deck.
Porto alone shows 150 years of bridge history across one river.

cards.title: El viento y Tacoma Narrows
cards.text: En 1940, el puente colgante de Tacoma Narrows, en EE. UU., se retorció hasta destruirse con un viento moderado debido a la inestabilidad aerodinámica. Desde entonces, los tableros se ensayan en túnel de viento y se diseñan para evitarlo.

deep.x: In November 1940, the Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington State twisted itself apart in a wind of about 64 km/h, just months after opening.
Flutter, not simple resonance
The failure is often attributed to resonance, but engineers now describe it as aeroelastic flutter: the deck's motion changed the airflow in a way that kept adding energy.
Lessons
Filmed
The collapse was filmed and became one of the most famous engineering films ever, still used in teaching.
Bridges must be designed for how wind moves them, not just how hard it blows.

cards.title: Juntas de dilatación
cards.text: Los puentes se alargan y se acortan con la temperatura. Las juntas de dilatación (los dientes metálicos por los que pasas con el coche) y los apoyos deslizantes les permiten moverse sin agrietarse.

deep.x: Bridges expand and contract with temperature, and move under traffic and wind. Expansion joints and bearings allow this movement safely.
How much movement
Bearings
Maintenance
Joints suffer from traffic impact, debris and water. Damaged joints let water reach bearings and steel, causing corrosion.
The clatter as you drive over a joint is the bridge breathing.

cards.title: Cimentaciones en ríos

steps: La crecida acelera junto a la pila

cards.text: Las pilas en los ríos deben resistir la socavación: el agua rápida que excava el lecho a su alrededor. Muchos fallos de puentes se deben a la socavación durante las crecidas, no a la propia estructura.

deep.x: Bridge piers in rivers must resist scour: fast-flowing water digging away the riverbed around foundations.
Entre-os-Rios

On 4 March 2001, the Hintze Ribeiro Bridge over the Douro at Entre-os-Rios collapsed during floods, killing 59 people. Scour around a pier, aggravated by sand extraction from the river, was identified as a key factor.
Protection
After the disaster
The tragedy led to major changes in Portuguese bridge inspection and management.
Many bridges fall because of what happens under the water.

cards.title: Inspección y mantenimiento

items: Control de corrosión en cables y armaduras

cards.text: Los puentes se inspeccionan con regularidad en busca de grietas, corrosión, desgaste de los apoyos y socavación. Cada vez más, unos sensores vigilan en tiempo real las deformaciones, las vibraciones y los movimientos.

deep.x: Bridges need regular inspection and maintenance throughout their lives, often 100 years or more.
Inspection levels
Structural health monitoring
Genoa 2018
The collapse of Genoa's Morandi Bridge in August 2018, killing 43 people, intensified attention on ageing bridges and maintenance across Europe.
Bridges last a century only with a century of care.

quiz.q: ¿Qué tipo de puente soporta las cargas principalmente a compresión?
quiz.explain: Los arcos llevan las cargas a los estribos.

quiz.q: El puente 25 de Abril de Lisboa es un…
quiz.explain: Los cables principales cuelgan de las torres.

quiz.q: ¿Qué destruyó el puente de Tacoma Narrows en 1940?
options: Oscilaciones de torsión provocadas por el viento
quiz.explain: Inestabilidad aerodinámica.

lessons.title: Edificios y cimentaciones
lessons.summary: Desde el suelo hacia arriba.

cards.title: ¿Para qué sirven las cimentaciones?
cards.text: Las cimentaciones reparten el peso de un edificio sobre un suelo capaz de soportarlo sin hundirse de forma desigual. Cuanto más débil es el suelo, más grandes o profundas son las cimentaciones.

deep.x: Foundations transfer a building's loads safely to the ground, spreading them so the soil isn't overloaded and the building doesn't settle unevenly.
Soil strength
Site investigation
Design choice
The weaker the soil, the larger or deeper the foundations must be, sometimes reaching down tens of metres to firm layers.
A building is only as good as the ground it stands on.

cards.title: Cimentaciones superficiales
cards.text: Las zapatas corridas y aisladas, o una losa de cimentación, funcionan donde hay suelo firme o roca cerca de la superficie. Son habituales en viviendas.

deep.x: Shallow foundations sit near the surface where good soil or rock is close. They're common for houses and low buildings.
Frost and moisture
Foundations must go below the depth affected by seasonal drying, frost or tree roots. In Portugal frost is rarely an issue, but clay shrinkage can be.
Raft foundations
On good ground, simple footings do the job.

cards.title: Cimentaciones profundas
cards.text: En terreno blando, los pilotes se hincan o se perforan hasta capas más firmes y soportan las cargas por la punta y por el rozamiento lateral. La Baixa de Lisboa se reconstruyó después de 1755 sobre pilotes de madera.

deep.x: Where surface soils are weak, piles carry loads down to stronger layers or develop resistance through friction along their length.

items: rest on rock or dense layers
rely on soil grip along their sides

deep.x: Pile types
Lisbon's Baixa
After the 1755 earthquake, the Baixa Pombalina was rebuilt on reclaimed, waterlogged ground using pine piles. Kept below the water table, wood resists rot for centuries.
Groundwater risk

items.w: Lowering the water table near old wooden piles
items.r: Monitor and protect: exposed piles can rot

deep.x: Piles reach past weak ground to something solid.

cards.title: Asientos

items.w: una esquina sobre relleno blando
items.r: cimentar más hondo allí

items.w: grietas que se abren
items.r: vigilar e investigar

cards.text: Todos los edificios se asientan un poco. Los problemas vienen del asiento diferencial, cuando una parte se hunde más que otra, lo que agrieta muros y atasca puertas.

deep.x: All buildings settle slightly as the soil compresses. Problems arise when settlement is uneven.

items.w: Some settlement means failure
items.r: Uniform settlement is normal, differential settlement causes damage

deep.x: Signs of differential settlement

items: Diagonal cracks near doors and windows

deep.x: Causes

items.b: soft and firm areas under one building

deep.x: The Leaning Tower of Pisa
Even settlement is fine; uneven settlement cracks walls.

cards.title: Muros y estructuras

items: pilares y vigas soportan las cargas

cards.text: Los edificios tradicionales tienen muros de carga de piedra o ladrillo. Los modernos usan estructuras de pilares y vigas de hormigón o acero, y los muros solo rellenan los huecos.

deep.x: Buildings carry loads either through load-bearing walls or through frames of columns and beams.

items: concrete or steel columns and beams

deep.x: Traditional Portuguese buildings
Many older Portuguese buildings have thick stone or brick walls with timber floors. Later ones, from the mid-20th century, use reinforced concrete frames.
Renovation caution

items.w: Knocking through walls in old buildings
items.r: Check first: walls may carry the floors above

deep.x: Frame advantages
Know whether walls hold up the building or just divide rooms.

cards.title: La jaula pombalina

steps: Jaula de madera en los muros

cards.text: Tras el terremoto de 1755, Lisboa se reconstruyó con la «gaiola pombalina»: un entramado de madera con riostras diagonales dentro de los muros de mampostería, uno de los primeros sistemas constructivos sismorresistentes de Europa.

deep.x: After the 1755 earthquake destroyed much of Lisbon, the city was rebuilt with an innovative earthquake-resistant system: the "gaiola pombalina".

steps: Timber frame of uprights and diagonals

deep.x: Who built it
The reconstruction under the Marquis of Pombal was led by engineers and architects including Manuel da Maia, Eugénio dos Santos and Carlos Mardel.
The marching test
According to historical accounts, troops marched around a model of the timber cage to simulate an earthquake and test its resistance.
Legacy
The Pombaline Baixa is often cited as one of the first examples of large-scale earthquake-resistant urban construction in the world.

cards.title: Diseño sismorresistente

items: Aislamiento en la base para edificios clave

cards.text: Las normas sísmicas exigen que los edificios se balanceen sin derrumbarse: uniones dúctiles, arriostramientos, muros de cortante, formas regulares. Algunos usan aisladores en la base que dejan que el suelo se mueva bajo ellos.

deep.x: Seismic design aims to let buildings sway and deform without collapsing, protecting lives even in strong earthquakes.
Principles

items.b: beams yield first, columns stay standing

deep.x: Base isolation

steps: Rubber and steel bearings under building

deep.x: Portugal
Portugal applies the European seismic code (Eurocode 8). Many older buildings in Lisbon predate modern codes, making seismic retrofitting a priority.
Buildings can't stop earthquakes; they can survive them.

cards.title: El viento en los edificios altos
cards.text: El viento empuja los edificios altos y los hace oscilar. Los ingenieros los rigidizan con núcleos y estabilizadores, y algunos rascacielos usan enormes amortiguadores de masa sintonizada para contrarrestar el movimiento.

deep.x: Wind loads grow rapidly with height and can make tall buildings sway uncomfortably. Engineers stiffen and dampen them.
Solutions

items.b: concrete shafts for lifts and stairs

deep.x: Taipei 101
Taipei 101 has a 660-tonne steel ball suspended near its top as a tuned mass damper, visible to visitors.
Comfort
People feel sway long before it's dangerous. Designers limit accelerations to avoid motion sickness in occupants.
Tall buildings are designed to sway safely, and then dampened so you don't notice.

cards.title: Humedad

items: Tejado y remates en buen estado

cards.text: El agua es la enemiga de los edificios: la humedad por capilaridad, las goteras y la condensación causan podredumbre, moho y corrosión. Las barreras antihumedad, los buenos tejados, los canalones y la ventilación la mantienen fuera.

deep.x: Water is one of the biggest threats to buildings, causing rot, mould, corrosion and damage to finishes.
Types of damp

items.b: moist indoor air on cold surfaces

deep.x: Portugal's challenge
Many Portuguese homes suffer condensation and mould in winter, because of poor insulation, cold surfaces and limited heating and ventilation.
Solutions
Keep water out, let moisture out.

cards.title: Burj Khalifa
cards.text: El edificio más alto del mundo, en Dubái, mide 828 m. Su planta en forma de Y y sus retranqueos desorientan al viento, y su cimentación incluye 192 pilotes de unos 50 m de largo.

deep.x: Dubai's Burj Khalifa, completed in 2010, is the world's tallest building at 828 m.
Confusing the wind
The Y-shaped plan and spiralling setbacks change the building's shape with height, so wind vortices can't organise into a strong rhythm.
Structure
Records
What's next
Saudi Arabia's Jeddah Tower, under construction, aims to be the first building over 1 km tall.
Shape, not just strength, keeps the tallest tower standing.

quiz.q: ¿Qué es el asiento diferencial?
options: Que todas las partes se hundan por igual
Que una parte del edificio se hunda más que otra
quiz.explain: Provoca grietas.

quiz.q: ¿Qué era la gaiola pombalina?
options: Un entramado de madera dentro de los muros para resistir terremotos
quiz.explain: Se usó en la reconstrucción de Lisboa tras 1755.

quiz.q: ¿Cuándo se usan pilotes?
options: Sobre roca sólida cerca de la superficie
En terreno blando, para llegar a capas más firmes
quiz.explain: Transmiten las cargas a estratos más profundos.

lessons.title: Motores
lessons.summary: Cómo convierten los motores de gasolina y diésel el combustible en movimiento.

cards.title: El ciclo de cuatro tiempos
cards.text: La mayoría de los motores de coche repiten cuatro tiempos: aspirar aire y combustible, comprimirlos, encenderlos para que empujen el pistón y expulsar los gases de escape. «Admisión, compresión, explosión, escape».

deep.x: Most car engines run on the four-stroke cycle patented by Nikolaus Otto's company in 1876. Each cylinder repeats four piston strokes over two crankshaft turns.

steps: Power: spark ignites, piston pushed down

deep.x: "Suck, squeeze, bang, blow"

items.b: valves open, air and fuel drawn in
valves closed, pressure and temperature rise

deep.x: Only one stroke makes power
Three of the four strokes absorb energy. Multiple cylinders firing in sequence and a heavy flywheel keep rotation smooth.
Two-stroke engines
Four strokes, two turns, one bang per cylinder.

cards.title: Cigüeñal
cards.text: Los pistones suben y bajan; el cigüeñal convierte ese movimiento en rotación, como las piernas que empujan los pedales de una bici. Un volante de inercia suaviza los impulsos.

deep.x: The crankshaft converts the pistons' up-and-down motion into rotation, just as your legs turn bicycle pedals.
Engine layouts

items.b: cylinders in a row, most small cars
two banks in a V, compact for more cylinders
